An explicit port option must still win over the declared value. Two ways the surface loses information without saying so. FIRST, the restart command is documented as a shutdown followed by a serve, but it accepts fewer options than serve does: serve takes a walltime and a flag to disable speculative decoding, and restart takes neither, so restarting a serve that was launched with either silently drops it and the endpoint comes back configured differently from how it went down. Give restart every option serve accepts, so a restart can reproduce the serve it replaces. SECOND, the port-collision guard runs only on the submitting path: the dry-run branch returns before the guard, so a dry run of a serve whose port is already held prints a complete script and exits zero, and the operator discovers the refusal only when they submit for real. Since the entire point of a dry run here is to check before committing, run the guard on that path too and report the refusal without submitting anything. Tests assert restart accepts and forwards both options serve accepts, and that a dry run whose resolved port is already held reports the refusal and names the holder rather than printing a script. Do not change any sizing default or engine setting, and keep the submitting path's behaviour exactly as it is.

node_definition.done_when: imas-ambix agent serve deepseek-v4-1-flash --dry-run emits all three of: the environment variable PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF set to expandable_segments:True, --chunked-prefill-size 16384, and --max-running-requests 64. All three target the SAME measured constraint, which is why they ship together: a 203,241-token prefill consumes 37.1 GB of 40.65 GB free, and that is the caching allocator's high-water mark from transient prefill peaks rather than steady-state use. Expandable segments addresses the roughly 4.45 GiB the allocator reports as reserved-but-unallocated, a figure the OOM message printed along with that exact remedy. Halving the prefill chunk from 32768 halves the transient peak per chunk at some prefill-rate cost. The running-request bound drops from the engine default 256 to 64, which sits above the 32 concurrent already measured working so it leaves burst headroom, while cutting scheduling structures fourfold; requests beyond the bound QUEUE rather than fail because max_queued_requests is None, so no client sees an error. The first two are profile-only: chunked_prefill_size already exists on EngineConfig with default 32768, and engine.env already carries SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE so the allocator variable joins it there. The third needs a new EngineConfig field and an emitter, following the precedent set when enable_metrics was added to profile.py and slurm.py; keep it SGLang-only so the vLLM command stays byte-identical and PROVE that by diffing a deepseek-v4-flash dry-run before and after.
